summary: API Gateway 5xx elevation during ephemeral worker thaw and model swap causing degraded customer requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customer TextLoop reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) for API requests starting ~2026-03-12T22:10 UTC. Errors persisted for ~45 minutes with intermittent recovery windows. The spike coincided with an automated ephemeral worker thaw (scale-up) and a model variant swap on the serving cluster serving dedicated tenant traffic.

Impact:
- ~18% of TextLoop requests during the window returned 5xx (502/503).
- Mainly short chat/generation calls and medium-size embedding requests failed or timed out.
- Customer experienced degraded UX for a subset of users; no data loss reported.

Timeline (high level):
- 22:05 UTC: autoscaler initiated ephemeral worker thaw to meet tenant concurrency.
- 22:08 UTC: model swap to redwood/opt-6.7b-quant (variant pin rollout) began.
- 22:10–22:55 UTC: elevated 5xx observed; error rate peak at ~22:18 UTC.
- 22:40 UTC: mitigation (temporary route-weight shift away from new variant) applied; error rate decreased but transient spikes continued until 22:55 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (heuristic):
1. Simulate tenant concurrency ramp in prod us-west using representative request mix (chat + embeddings).
2. Trigger ephemeral worker warmup/thaw while rolling a model variant to the same serving pool.
3. Observe API gateway logs for 502/503 patterns and serving runtime restarts.

Observed logs / snippets:
- apigw: "upstream reset while reading response header from upstream" / 502 at 22:18:03
- apigw: "503 Service Unavailable - no healthy upstreams for route" spikes correlated with accept-queue growth
- runtime: "watchdog: worker killed due to NVML reset during prefetch" and "prefetch-lock timeout: shard=7"
- ephemeral-scheduler: "thaw: provisioning 6 workers, delay waiting for kvcache warmup"

Initial hypothesis:
Concurrent effects: (A) ephemeral worker thaw increased accept queue pressure on proxy layer while workers warmed KV caches; (B) a model variant swap introduced heavier prefetch and KV-lock contention causing upstream runtime slowdowns and occasional watchdog resets; (C) apigw backpressure policy then amplified the symptom into short 5xx waves.
investigation_notes:
Investigators: Tomás (SRE), Lina (runtime), Aaron (support). Verified correlation between model-swap window and 5xx spike via traces in datadog and per-tenant token-level telemetry. Key findings:
- Accept-queue length on apigw increased by 3.2x during thaw; p95 request queue latency rose from 8ms to 120ms.
- Runtime instances handling new variant showed elevated prefetch stall events (kv shard lock). The lock hold times spiked from ~5ms to >200ms.
- Two runtime workers experienced NVML resets (driver-level) within the window; process restarts caused temporary upstream unavailability.
- Circuit-breaker configs were marginally tuned for steady-state and did not handle simultaneous thaw+swap well.
Observations logged to incident channel #incidents-support and linked PR added for telemetry improvements. Hypothesis prioritized: kvcache prefetch lock amplification + accept-queue starve -> 5xx spikes.

resolution:
Mitigation applied (temporary routing away from newly-swapped variant + autoscaler guardrail to avoid thaw+swap on same pool). Runtime hotfix PR merged to add prefetch-lock timeouts and more granular KV-shard metrics; rollout scheduled to canary in us-west (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1142).
Follow-ups assigned:
- SRE: formalize autoscaler guardrail (INT-803) to prevent concurrent thaw+swap; add unit/integration test.
- Runtime: complete canary rollout and monitor prefetch-lock metrics, implement graceful degradation path if prefetch stalls >100ms.
- DevEx: surface tenant-level retry guidance to customers and add note to Runbook.
Customer impact resolved for this event; recommend postmortem within 1 week and telemetry addition to detect accept-queue growth earlier.
